newsitem.title: UK: India sugar policy could cause higher world prices.
newsitem.headline: India sugar policy could cause higher world prices.

text.p: World sugar prices could see a dramatic upward reversal in 1997 if key producer India suffers a deficit from its domestic liberalisation policy, brokerage GNI said on Tuesday.
In its February report, GNI said the market's long-term concern would be the effect that domestic liberalisation would have on output and consumption.
"It is quite possible that the country could find itself in a deficit situation in 1997/98, which would have the effect of significantly tightening the world market place," GNI said.
"Sugar could see a dramatic reversal in 1997."
Last month India approved an ordinance to end the monopoly of the Indian Sugar and General Industries Import-Export Corp (ISGIEC) on exports and allowing more firms to export sugar.
GNI said the end of the monopoly was certainly likely to herald an increase in exports from the country but sales would probably not be massive.
With the world expected to be in oversupply again in 1997, further price falls were likely, it added.
